chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ibn Bukayr, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the person in janabah: may he eat, drink, and recite the Qur'an? He said: “Yes, he may eat, drink, recite the Qur'an, and remember Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as much as he wishes.”

key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in the state of janabah, requiring ghusl
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic; honorific for Allah

ai.seo_question: Can a person in janabah eat, drink, recite the Qur'an, and do dhikr before ghusl?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a person in the state of janabah is permitted to eat, drink, recite the Qur'an, and engage in dhikr of Allah عزّ وجلّ. It serves as a jurisprudential ruling clarifying what remains permissible before ghusl from janabah.
